targetEvidence.finding: SSR verifies a session and keeps data params empty by default; signed-out dynamic chat, news-edit, wallet, disable, and plan shells reduce layout paths to static collections so breadcrumbs and return URLs cannot disclose route references; payment intents, the admin news list, the redacted global notification inventory, and the redacted audit inventory perform normalized authenticated reads with explicit non-empty, empty, forbidden where applicable, unavailable, or malformed outcomes.

The read-only compatibility adapter targets the pinned Rust backend's protected admin-news contract, caps declared and chunked response bodies at 8 MiB before JSON allocation, rejects duplicate or malformed recognized query values and structural or semantic response drift, projects away bodies and identity/media fields, and never treats dependency or error envelopes as an authoritative empty list. The public file-backed content feed is deliberately not used as admin state.

The admin adapter forwards only a verified bearer and request ID to the exact global-list endpoint, fixes the page size at 20, caps declared and chunked bodies at 256 KiB, rejects structural and semantic drift, and projects only bounded delivery metadata. It distinguishes authoritative empty, recoverable out-of-range, forbidden, unavailable, and malformed outcomes without forwarding caller identity headers.

anchors: ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2
SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY
admin notification inventory contains invalid stored fields
targetEvidence.finding: The notification service owns a deterministic global read with strict limit/offset parsing and a redacted DTO. Count and page rows share one read-only repeatable-read transaction, and impossible cardinality, count failures, or invalid stored fields fail closed; recipients, users, templates, bodies, arbitrary data, error details, read state, and action URLs are never selected into the response.

The direct notification service admits only the exact GET admin/list shape after verifying the admin audience and canonical admin:notifications:manage permission; method, arity, and encoded-path drift fail closed before the handler.

The authenticated management page renders only the strict redacted projection with native pagination and retry links. It distinguishes ready, authoritative empty, forbidden, unavailable, malformed, and out-of-range recovery while emitting no identities, bodies, delivery errors, action URLs, forms, buttons, sample metrics, or mutation controls.

anchors: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY
ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT $4
targetEvidence.finding: The extracted analytics service owns an exact-audience, dedicated-permission read over only the canonical unified audit table. Startup validates the existing table shape, rows use stable keyset continuation in a read-only repeatable-read transaction, invalid stored fields fail the page, and the SELECT/DTO omit identity, target, network/device, before/after, and metadata fields.

The audit BFF adapter accepts only a closed category and bounded canonical cursor, follows no redirects, forwards only the verified bearer and request ID, caps declared and chunked bodies at 256 KiB, binds response rows to the requested category, validates newest-first unique summaries, rejects sensitive or unknown fields, and distinguishes ready, authoritative empty, forbidden, unavailable, and malformed outcomes.

The authenticated page independently validates the redacted projection and renders native category/keyset links, responsive labelled summary rows, semantic timestamps, and explicit outcome recovery without rendering record IDs, actor/target identity, details, export, forms, or mutations; the current reversible continuation token still carries the audit UUID and remains an explicit blocker.
The payments proxy is wired to the canonical typed admin-wide intent read; other proxy handlers generally remain disconnected from their page payloads.
The BFF preserves a closed safe status set and explicit dependency classes without forwarding upstream details, but still returns bare statuses rather than a typed error envelope consumed by pages.

The dispatcher validates route shape and extracts dynamic params, and signed-out dynamic chat, news-edit, wallet, disable, and plan skeletons use only static collection return paths so route references are not disclosed before authentication; route presence is still not live-data or mutation proof.

In-process tests prove only that the current GET targets are fixed and query input cannot choose an external target. Auth is a pre-SSR 307, notifications remains a 200 script document, and wallet management remains a pre-SSR 308; source middleware cookie, logout, session-ordering, method/cache, and browser parity remain open.

redirects.sourceSemantics: Pinned middleware clears cookies for logout, reason=no-session, and clear before the page-level redirect; otherwise the pinned page redirects to root
redirects.blocker: The fixed pre-SSR 307 removes the open redirect and matches the page destination, but source cookie clearing plus logout/session ordering, a pinned method/body/cache matrix, and authenticated browser/history/RSC/client-navigation proof remain absent.

redirects.sourceSemantics: Pinned Next.js page-level redirect() runs only after source middleware logout/session/admin-verification decisions
redirects.blocker: Replace or formally accept the 200 script transport only after authenticated browser/history/RSC/client-navigation proof, a pinned-origin method/body/cache matrix, and source middleware/logout/session ordering parity.

redirects.sourceSemantics: Pinned Next.js page-level redirect() runs only after source middleware logout/session/admin-verification decisions
redirects.blocker: The pre-SSR 308 target is fixed, but permanence and bypass ordering are not source parity until authenticated browser/history/RSC/client-navigation proof, a pinned-origin method/body/cache matrix, and source middleware/logout/session ordering parity exist.

stopBlockers: Most admin routes still lack an authoritative SSR service response; only bounded payment intents, protected legacy news, the redacted global notification inventory, and the redacted audit inventory currently populate typed PageContext data.
Sample rows, counts, timestamps, wallet addresses, balances, and health values can masquerade as live operational data.
Generic skeleton overlays are visual-capture fixtures, not loading-state contracts.
Ordinary Dioxus event closures are not usable in SSR output without proven hydration or a browser bridge.
Dynamic chat, news, wallet, disable, and plan identifiers need strict decode, length, grammar, and canonicalization rules.
Read and manage permissions must be split per operation and rechecked by the owning Rust service for every mutation.
BFF route protection proves authentication only; it does not prove downstream operation authorization.
BFF error responses remain bare statuses without stable codes, validation details, retryability, or correlation, and admin pages do not consume the preserved status semantics.
Forms are not accepted until method, content type, body, response envelope, redirect, and error behavior match an implemented endpoint.
No durable pending, success, error, retry, conflict, or rollback UX is proven for admin mutations.
List search, filtering, sorting, and pagination must survive refresh and back/forward navigation and remain backend-driven.
Owner-scoped wallet and subscription reads must reject or non-leakingly hide foreign resources.
Payment and credit controls cannot report success before A6 finality, idempotency, and durable ledger evidence.
Plan editing cannot duplicate A4/A9 policy or derive eligibility, pricing, entitlements, or ranking rules in the UI.
News and media operations cannot close before A10 publication, revision, validation, storage, and cache behavior are authoritative.
Chat, notification, analytics, media, and audit surfaces remain dependent on A11 service contracts.
Every route needs authenticated browser proof at mobile and desktop widths, keyboard operation, focus restoration, and overflow checks.
Every data or mutation path needs correlation, audit event, metrics/log redaction, timeout, retry, and recovery evidence under A12.
The three intentional redirects still need authenticated browser/history/RSC/client-navigation proof, a pinned-origin method/body/cache matrix, and source middleware/logout/session ordering parity.
Production readiness remains STOP until all 27 routes are aligned and every route and global blocker is cleared.
